standard_prerequisites.name: Universal property of suspensions
standard_prerequisites.statement: susp A -> B is equivalent to the type of triples (b_n, b_s, A -> (b_n = b_s)), with the map from right to left given by the suspension recursor.
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the first equivalence of the chain at source lines 687-688 and is invoked again at source lines 693-695.

standard_prerequisites.name: Associativity and commutation of sigma types
standard_prerequisites.statement: Sigma types reassociate and their components may be reordered without changing the type up to equivalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: Source lines 689-691 and 703-704 are consecutive reassociations of a four-component sigma type.

standard_prerequisites.name: Contractibility of the based path space
standard_prerequisites.statement: For any b_0 : B the type (Sigma b : B, b = b_0) is contractible with centre (b_0, refl b_0).
standard_prerequisites.use: It removes that component at source line 697 and again at source line 707.

core_obligations: Unfold Map_*(susp A, B) as pairs (f, f(north) = b_0) and rewrite susp A -> B by the universal property of suspensions as (b_n, b_s, A -> (b_n = b_s)) with the recursor as the backwards map (source lines 685-695).

Reassociate the resulting sigma type, reorder its components and use the contractibility of (Sigma b_n, b_n = b_0) to drop that component, reducing to Sigma b_s : B, A -> (b_0 = b_s) (source lines 687-697).
In the second chain, expand again by adding a pair (q, g(a_0) = q) and reassociate, so that the same contractibility can be applied a second time (source lines 700-704).
Recognise the resulting type Sigma g : A -> (b_0 = b_0), g(a_0) = refl b_0 as definitionally Map_*(A, Omega B), closing the equivalence (source lines 704-707).

proof_roadmap.step: First chain: unfold pointed maps out of the suspension and rewrite by the suspension universal property, reassociating sigma types.
Justify each step: the suspension recursor, associativity of sigma, and contractibility of the based path space.
Second chain: re-expand, apply the same contractibility again, and read off Map_*(A, Omega B).

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.5.4 at source lines 678-682: for pointed types (A,a_0) and (B,b_0) the pointed mapping space Map_*(susp A, B) is equivalent to Map_*(A, Omega B). The author's proof (source lines 684-708) is a two-stage computation of equivalences, not a citation: the first chain at lines 686-692 rewrites susp A -> B by the suspension universal property, then reassociates a four-component sigma type three times, and the individual steps are justified afterwards at lines 693-697 by the suspension recursor, by associativity of sigma types and by the contractibility of the based path space. The second chain at lines 700-706 must re-expand with an extra pair (q, g(a_0) = q) before the same contractibility can be applied again, and only the final line is the definitional identification with Map_*(A, Omega B).
